newsitem.title: UK: Greenpeace says it kept radioactive sand in yard.
newsitem.headline: Greenpeace says it kept radioactive sand in yard.

text.p: The environmental pressure group Greenpeace admitted on Sunday storing radioactive contaminated sand in oil drums at its London headquarters.
Campaigners, reacting to media reports, insisted the drums were properly stored in its backyard and posed no health risk.
The sand samples were taken from beaches near the English nuclear power plant at Sellafield.
A Greenpeace spokesman defended the move, saying: "It is far better to have this sand properly and safely stored in our own yard than to simply dump it on a rubbish tip."
"In our view, yes this sand is contaminated, but only at very low levels and is not any different to the sand that lies on the public beaches around Sellafield.
"It has all been double-bagged and sealed in these oil drums. There is absolutely no health risk or danger to the public."
Britain's Environmental Agency said it would be contacting Greenpeace for details of its storage.
"At the moment we do not have sufficient details to know if these drums contain anything which could be classed as low-level radioactive waste," a spokeswoman said.
"We will speak to Greenpeace tomorrow to establish all the facts and will carry out a site inspection if we feel it is necessary," she said.
